### Release: A fair go for families

By LabourVoices

01 October 2026

documents/release-a-fair-go-for-kiwi-dri.title: Release: A fair go for Kiwi drivers
documents/release-a-fair-go-for-kiwi-dri.text:
##### Release: A fair go for Kiwi drivers

Labour will make car repairs cheaper, crack down on unfair fuel prices and bring more competition to the pump, putting drivers back in the driver’s seat.

"This election is about the cost of living. For most Kiwis, a car is a necessity, it's how we get to work, drop the kids at school, and get on with life,” Labour leader Chris Hipkins said.

“But under National, the cost of getting around keeps climbing. Labour will give drivers a fair go, whether they’re buying a car, fixing it or filling it up.

“We’ll crack down on price gouging, freeze fuel tax for three years and make it easier for independent mechanics and petrol stations to compete,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

Give drivers the right to repair. Require carmakers to give independent mechanics fair access to the manuals, software, tools and information needed to fix modern cars.

Put fuel prices under the microscope. Require the Commerce Commission to report weekly on fuel prices and whether falling costs are being passed on to drivers.

Crack down on fuel price gouging. Apply Labour’s price gouging law to wholesale and retail fuel, allowing unfair pricing to be investigated and overcharges recovered.

Open up the fuel market. Give independent petrol stations fairer access to fuel supplies and stronger protection against restrictive contracts.

Make more room for competition. Require NZTA to consider making surplus land available for independent unmanned petrol stations and EV chargers.

“Your car belongs to you. You should be able to choose who fixes it,” Labour Commerce and Consumer Affairs spokesperson Arena Williams said.

"A right to repair means the mechanic down the road gets a fair shot at your business. It backs local workshops, supports skilled jobs and apprenticeships, and gives drivers a real choice.

“Currently independent workshops have to turn away work because they can't access the information they need to make repairs - Labour will fix this. Australia already did this in 2022 and has led to independent mechanics there able to repair cars 25% cheaper on average than dealerships.

"And we’re bringing in more competition at the pump too. The Commerce Commission found that fuel prices rise faster than they fall, costing Kiwi drivers around $15 million a year. When we were in government, Labour forced the big fuel companies to publish their wholesale prices and opened the market up to independent stations. Now we're going further.

"Labour's price gouging law will apply to fuel. We're giving the Commerce Commission the powers it needs to report fuel prices every week and make sure that when wholesale fuel costs fall, drivers see it at the pump.

“National is driving up prices – we can't afford another three years of their hidden costs and higher prices. Whether you’re buying your car, fixing it, or filling it up, Labour will make sure Kiwi drivers get a fair go,” Arena Williams said.

Stay in the loop by signing up to our mailing list and following us on Facebook, Instagram, and X.

### Release: A fair go for Kiwi drivers

By LabourVoices

05 October 2026

documents/release-a-labour-government-wi.title: Release: A Labour Government will not join AUKUS
documents/release-a-labour-government-wi.text:
##### Release: A Labour Government will not join AUKUS

New Zealand will not sign up to the nuclear-powered pillar one, or the pillar two of AUKUS under a Labour Government.

“Our country has a fiercely independent foreign policy, and a Government I lead will not join pillars one or two of AUKUS,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“We are proud to stand apart and lead the world being nuclear-free, that is not going to change now.

“Labour is deeply concerned about how much time and effort this Government has spent getting closer to the US over the past year, when we spent six years in government diversifying New Zealand’s trade interests and staunchly defending our right to be independent.

“New Zealand’s foreign policy will not be determined by Washington, Canberra or Beijing.

“I look forward to continuing to build strong relationships with leaders and nations as Prime Minister in 2026, but I refuse to do it on a nuclear-adjacent platform,” Chris Hipkins said.

“Our foreign policy is based on principles,” Labour foreign affairs spokesperson David Parker said.

“This does not mean we are non-aligned. We are a liberal western democracy and share those precious values with others. We support the rules-based order. We are part of Five Eyes, which we also value.

“New Zealand’s interests lie in trade, peace, and in on-going diplomacy, not in being a ‘force-multiplier’ for one super-power in a containment strategy directed against another,” David Parker said.

##### Release: Getting kids off screens and back to being kids

Labour will make it easier for kids to get off screens and back to being kids, with more affordable after-school activities, healthier boundaries in schools and better support for parents to keep their children safe online.

“Too much of childhood is being spent on screens, while sport, hobbies and other after-school activities are out of reach for too many families,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Parents are struggling to navigate the risks of the online world, and young people are telling us they want action on harmful content and the impact it’s having on their lives.

“Labour is listening. We want kids to have more opportunities to get out, get active, make friends, and enjoy being kids while making sure they’re safer online.

“Our Kids Off Screens plan will give families more affordable alternatives, help schools set healthier boundaries around screens, and give parents better tools to protect their children online.

“Technology has its place, but it shouldn’t come at the expense of childhood. New Zealand is the best place in the world to raise children, and I want us to keep it that way,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour's Kids Off Screens policy will focus on three areas:

- Affordable activities: Boost funding for community sports and activity grants to make after-school activities more affordable for families.
- Right screen, right time: Introduce healthier boundaries around screen use for kids, in partnership with experts, schools and young people.
- Back parents to keep kids safe: helping parents make informed choices through accessible online safety tools and supporting schools to use technology safely with an education AI app.

The policy complements Labour's AI Action Plan, which includes reviewing existing laws to strengthen protections against online harm, supporting schools to use artificial intelligence safely, and establishing an independent online regulator.

“Keeping kids safe online isn't about turning back the clock or pretending technology doesn't have a place in our lives. It's about preparing for the future and making sure our schools, laws and protections keep pace with the world our children are growing up in," Labour education spokesperson Ginny Andersen said.

“Building on expert recommendations made to the Government in 2024, Labour will work with educators, health experts, and young people to get the balance right in our schools and kura.

“Kids need to be able to concentrate on learning, build friendships and develop the social skills that will serve them throughout their lives.

“Our children deserve a future where technology works for them, not one where they are left to deal with its risks alone. Labour is ready to take action," Ginny Andersen said.

documents/release-labour-backs-community.title: Release: Labour backs community housing to build more homes
documents/release-labour-backs-community.text:
##### Release: Labour backs community housing to build more homes

Labour will raise the Crown guarantee for Community Housing Funding Agency (CHFA) Social Bonds, helping community housing providers build more homes by lowering the cost of finance.

“After three years of neglect, New Zealand's housing shortage is getting worse. One of the fastest and most effective ways to build more homes is to reduce the cost of finance for the organisations already doing the work,” Labour housing spokesperson Kieran McAnulty said.

“This is a Crown guarantee, similar to the guarantee provided to banks, that would only be called on in the unlikely event of a default. The community housing sector was hoping the current Government would provide this guarantee. They didn’t, but Labour will.

“Combined with further reductions in CHFA lending margins, the guarantee is expected to cut borrowing costs by around half a percentage point from day one.

“By enabling AAA-rated borrowing, interest rates for housing providers are cut, and those savings are invested in building more homes. The maths is straightforward, the CHFA estimate for every 11 homes built, the financing efficiency could pay for a twelfth, at no additional cost to the taxpayer.

“That means more homes can be built with the same investment. Every dollar saved on interest is a dollar that can go into building homes and supporting tenants.

“This will back the organisations already delivering affordable housing across New Zealand, including charities, iwi, Pacific and disability organisations, and providers of public housing, transitional housing, affordable rentals, accessible homes and housing for older people.

“Community housing providers are ready to build. What they need is a Labour government willing to back them.

“The $950 million guarantee would come into effect from Labour's first Budget in Government in 2027.

“This policy will help get more affordable homes built faster, so more New Zealanders can access the housing they need,” Kieran McAnulty said.

##### Release: Labour backs family doctors

Labour’s new Family Doctor Loan Scheme will support doctors and nurse practitioners with low-interest loans to set up new practices or buy into existing ones.

- Loans only available for owner and community-operated general practices

- The loans will be delivered through the existing Small Business Cashflow Loan Scheme

“Nearly 650,000 New Zealanders can’t afford to see their doctor when they need to, and many others wait too long for an appointment.

“This announcement builds on our plan for three free doctor’s visits, improvements to GP funding, and free cervical screening – all aimed at making it easier for people to get care when they need it.

“The number of doctor-owned practices is falling, as is the number of doctors who work in doctor-owned practices. It’s expensive to start a new practice or buy into an existing one, so our low-interest loans will give doctors the kick start they need to get established.

“Two-thirds of practice owners and partners are intending to retire in the next 10 years, so it’s vital we can support the next generation to keep the doors and books open.

##### Release: Labour Bill helps renters save on energy costs

Labour MP Helen White’s Member’s Bill to make landlords provide curtains in rental homes has been pulled from the Biscuit Tin today, offering a practical way to cut power bills for renters as energy prices soar under the National Government.

The Residential Tenancies (Requiring Landlords to Provide Curtains) Amendment Bill would require landlords to provide insulated curtains or window coverings in rental properties.

"Curtains might sound like a small thing, but up to 30 percent of energy loss in an insulated home escapes through uncovered windows," Helen White said.

"Right now, renters already struggling with the high cost of living are being doubly hit with additional costs: once if they buy and install window coverings, and again through higher power costs.”

The Bill would extend the existing healthy homes standards to include window coverings, making it the responsibility of landlords to provide them, rather than tenants.

“Because curtains are a fixture that stays in the home, it is logical that landlords, not tenants, supply window coverings that can help with insulation.

"With energy prices up nearly 20 percent under this Government, this Bill is practical way that we can put some money back in renters’ pockets.

“On the same day that National announced they are increasing rents for the country's most vulnerable, my Bill is all about on lowering costs for renters.

“I look forward to debating my Bill in the House and urge my colleagues in Parliament to support it,” Helen White said.

Labour will invest in Māori-led training to help more people gain skills, get into good work and earn more.

##### Release: Labour is backing small business to grow

Labour is giving Kiwi small businesses a fair go - ensuring they get paid sooner, can invest in the equipment they need, and keep more of what they earn.

“Small businesses are the heart of New Zealand's economy, contributing around 42% of our GDP,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Small business owners take the risks, put in the hours, employ locally and keep our communities running. But under National, they’re being squeezed by rising costs and falling demand.

“Business liquidations are at a 15-year high, business confidence is falling and Christopher Luxon is telling hardworking business owners they’re too soft and to grow up.

“Under a Labour Government, small business owners will get paid sooner, get more support to invest in the equipment they need, and keep more of what they earn,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour's Small Business Action Plan – A Fair Go will:

- Require big businesses to pay small suppliers within 15 days
  on invoices of $25,000 or less and to publish how quickly they pay their suppliers.
- Lift the asset write-off from $1,000 to $10,000
  for businesses with annual turnover below $10 million, so small businesses can immediately deduct the cost of new equipment from their tax bill.
- Raise the GST registration threshold from $60,000 to $80,000 meaning around 35,000 of the smallest operators will no longer have to register for GST.

“Running a small business should mean building something of your own, not spending your evenings chasing overdue invoices and filling in forms,” Labour Small Business spokesperson Dan Rosewarne said.

“If you’re a tradie waiting months for a corporate to pay an invoice, a café owner replacing an oven, or a mechanic upgrading equipment, these changes are about giving you a fair go.

“Lifting the asset write-off means a small business can invest in the tools and equipment it needs now, rather than waiting years to claim the full cost. Raising the GST threshold means around 35,000 of the smallest operators can spend less time on tax returns and more time running their businesses and gives small businesses more room to grow.

“These are simple, easy measures a Labour government will take to support the small businesses that keep New Zealand’s economy ticking,” Dan Rosewarne said.

##### Release: Labour’s plan to grow the economy from the grassroots up

Labour has released its economic plan to create growth and opportunity in every part of the country, with good jobs, a fair go for small businesses, and a new commitment to back Kiwi companies through Elevate.

“Kiwis deserve an economy where hard work gets you ahead,” Labour finance and economy spokesperson Barbara Edmonds said.

“Right now, too many people are working harder just to stand still. Wages aren’t keeping up, the weekly shop costs more, and small businesses are doing it tough.

“Three years on from National’s promise to get things moving, 171,000 Kiwis are out of work, business liquidations are at a 15-year high, and 2,000 people are leaving the country every week. National had its chance, and families are worse off for it.

"Labour has a plan to turn that around. We’ll get Kiwis back into work, back small and innovative businesses to succeed, and bring everyday costs under control.

“And we’ll do it responsibly. Every dollar the government spends is someone’s hard earned money. We’ll treat it that way, managing the books carefully and investing where it makes a difference,” Barbara Edmonds said.

Labour will:

- Back innovative Kiwi companies by redirecting up to $50 million a year into Elevate
- Make big businesses pay small suppliers within 15 days
- Let small businesses claim new tools and equipment straight away, up to $10,000
- Raise the GST threshold to $80,000, giving small businesses more room to grow
- Give smaller Kiwi businesses a fairer chance to win government contracts
- Help small businesses and start-ups use AI to save time and get ahead
- Get Kiwis back into work fixing schools and hospitals and building homes
- Back 30,000 apprentices with an expanded apprenticeship boost, introducing a $1,000 tools grant, and guarantee every eligible graduate nurse a job
- Introduce a simple, targeted capital gains tax on investment and commercial property, with every dollar going to healthcare
- Establish the New Zealand Future Fund to invest in Kiwi businesses and infrastructure
- Return the books to surplus in 2028/29, bring back the Reserve Bank’s dual mandate, and set up an independent Parliamentary Budget Office.

“Labour is backing the people who keep our economy going,” Barbara Edmonds said.

“The tradie still waiting to be paid for a job finished months ago. The sole trader whose laptop gives out the week GST is due. The builder who just wants to get back on the tools.

“We’ll get them paid on time, help them invest in their business, and get work started right on their doorstep. When a local business wins a repair job, it keeps its team together, buys from nearby suppliers and takes on an apprentice.

“Labour will also back the Kiwi businesses that will create tomorrow’s jobs. Too many promising companies are forced to move or sell overseas before we see the full benefit.

“We’ll redirect up to $50 million a year of the Government’s contribution to the NZ Super Fund into Elevate, so more innovative businesses can expand, hire and pay good wages here at home.

“Government is about choices, and every commitment we’ve made is fully costed and paid for in our independently verified fiscal plan.

“This election is a choice between a country that cuts and a country that grows. Labour will deliver good jobs, a fair go and a future people can afford,” Barbara Edmonds said.

##### Release: Labour to accelerate climate action

A Labour government will fix the broken Emissions Trading Scheme as an urgent priority.

“New Zealand should be showing climate leadership; not going backwards as Christopher Luxon’s Government has done,” said Labour leader Chris Hipkins.

“The ETS is broken. The carbon price is too low to drive meaningful emissions reductions. Under National, climate pollution us the only thing that has got cheaper over the last three years.

“Current ETS rules also make it cheaper to plant exotic forests than to grow food. That doesn’t create jobs or help our economy.

“Labour will ensure the ETS Emissions Trading Scheme actually does what it is supposed to do and maintains a genuine price on emissions. We will restore credibility and certainty to the carbon market, generating revenues that can be invested in affordable energy and resilience.

“We will stop the short-term political tinkering that undermines business confidence and puts us all on the back foot.

“Labour is fully committed to the Paris Agreement and will put New Zealand on course to meet its targets. The Paris Agreement is essential for bringing countries together to address a problem affecting every country, every community and every generation. Walking away from it, as National and its mates are planning to do, would be giving up on our kids’ future and impose huge costs on our economy.

“We can’t afford another three years of National’s inaction on climate,” Chris Hipkins said.

“Labour will urgently review the ETS and move quickly to implement changes informed by this work,” Labour climate spokesperson Dr Deborah Russell said.

The review will:

· identify changes to incentivise genuine emissions reductions rather than relying on offsets,

· reconsider the role of forestry (as per PCE’s recommendation)

· ensure the ETS supports New Zealand’s Paris targets

· develop new rules to prevent whole-farm conversions.

· new forestry registrations in the ETS will be paused while this work is completed (as per PCE’s recommendation)

“New Zealanders deserve a government with a plan - one that understands climate action and economic growth go hand-in-hand.

“Climate change is one of the greatest challenges we face, but it is also one of the greatest opportunities available to New Zealand. We can deliver cleaner and more affordable energy, gives businesses the certainty to invest, and help our farmers to compete in global markets by building on New Zealand’s reputation for world class sustainability.

“Labour is committed to protecting our economy and growing our economy – creating good jobs, bringing down household costs and strengthening our energy security,” Dr Deborah Russell said.

##### Release: Labour to deliver unlimited public transport for $20-max a week

Labour will make it cheaper for New Zealanders to catch the bus or train, by capping weekly fares at just $20 in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, and $10 a week everywhere else in New Zealand.

"Our fare cap is a major cost-of-living commitment designed to put money back into the pockets of commuters, students and families," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

##### Release: Labour to ensure an immigration system that works for New Zealand

A Labour government will plan immigration around what New Zealand’s workforce, housing and infrastructure can support, and make sure migrants who commit to this country are backed to get ahead.

"Immigration should be planned around what New Zealand needs, and it should be managed in a way that's fair to everyone here and everyone who comes," Labour Immigration spokesperson Phil Twyford said.

“If you choose to build your life here, work here and raise your family here, a Labour government will back you to get ahead.

“Getting immigration right is fundamental to New Zealand’s future. We need an immigration system that attracts the skills and talent our country needs, protects migrants from exploitation, and gives people the confidence to build a future here,” Phil Twyford said.

Labour will:

- Plan immigration around New Zealand’s capacity by setting goals through a Government Policy Statement on immigration that reflects our workforce demographic, housing and infrastructure needs
- Encourage migrants to put down roots by extending the period migrants must live here before becoming eligible for permanent residence from two years to four, supported by a programme of New Zealand orientation and civic education delivered by community education providers to strengthen social cohesion.
- Protect migrants from exploitation by enabling migrants to move between accredited employers after three months, strengthening the Accredited Employer Work Visa scheme, and improving access to support in their communities.
- Treat people with decency by protecting humanitarian appeals against deportation, setting up a citizenship pathway for children born in New Zealand, and reviewing parent visa, health, and English-language rules.

“We should be ambitious about the contribution migrants can make to New Zealand, to our communities and to our economy, while making sure our immigration settings work for the country as a whole.

“That means having clear and predictable rules, protecting people from exploitation, and giving those who choose to make New Zealand their home a genuine opportunity to get ahead.

“Migrants bring skills, energy, and enterprise to New Zealand. A Labour government will back people to build their lives and careers here, while ensuring immigration supports the long-term interests of New Zealand,” Phil Twyford said.

documents/release-labour-to-give-kiwis-a.title: Release: Labour to give Kiwis a better deal when you fly
documents/release-labour-to-give-kiwis-a.text:
##### Release: Labour to give Kiwis a better deal when you fly

Labour will give Kiwis clearer prices, stronger passenger rights, and more choice when they fly.

“For many New Zealanders flying is how we get home for a birthday, get to a hospital appointment in another city, or keep a business running,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“But flying is expensive, and on many regional routes there is little or no competition. Kiwis are struggling with the cost of living and are finding it harder and harder to make those important trips. Only Labour has a real plan to tackle it across the economy.

“Labour will make prices more transparent, open opportunities for smaller airlines to compete and give passengers more rights.

“Kiwis deserve better prices, better protection and more choices when they fly,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Show the real price up front: Require airlines to show all-in, real-time airfares so Kiwis can properly compare the true cost of flights.
- Put passengers first: Require big airlines to provide automatic refunds when flights are cancelled or significantly changed, with compensation or reimbursement when checked baggage is significantly delayed or paid services aren’t delivered.
- Open the skies to more competition: Require fair access to essential airport infrastructure so smaller airlines can grow and compete.
- Make airlines more accountable: Require airlines to publicly report delays, cancellations and baggage performance, alongside greater scrutiny of fares, costs and profits.
- Keep airport costs under control: Make sure airports can raise capital and borrow cheaply, so essential infrastructure investment doesn’t unnecessarily push up airfares.

“For many regional routes there is limited or no competition. That means fewer choices for travellers and less pressure on airlines to offer better prices and service,” Labour commerce and consumer affairs spokesperson Arena Williams said.

“Smaller airlines shouldn’t have to compete with one hand tied behind their backs. Labour will give them fair access to the airport facilities they need to grow and connect regional New Zealand.

“We’ll make airlines more accountable, with greater scrutiny of fares, costs and profits and clear reporting on delays, cancellations and baggage.

“When an airline screws up, passengers shouldn’t have to fight to get their money back. If your flight is cancelled or significantly changed, you’ll get an automatic refund.

“Regional connections matter too. When an essential air service is at risk, Labour will bring the industry together to find long-term solutions to keep communities connected.

“National’s answer has been to hand smaller airlines a bit of extra cash to help them get by, while leaving the barriers to competition in place. That won’t help smaller airlines grow or give passengers more choice.

“Labour will open up competition, give smaller airlines a fair shot and give passengers enforceable rights when airlines let them down,” Arena Williams said.

documents/release-labour-to-give-parents.title: Release: Labour to give parents confidence in their children’s education
documents/release-labour-to-give-parents.text:
##### Release: Labour to give parents confidence in their children’s education

Labour will give parents confidence that their children are receiving a high-quality education built on evidence, expertise and long-term stability, rather than the political priorities of the Government of the day.

Labour Education spokesperson Ginny Andersen today announced plans for an Independent Council for Curriculum and Assessment (ICCA), which would provide expert leadership of New Zealand’s curriculum and assessment system.

“Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, and parents should be able to trust that what their children are learning is rigorous, evidence-based and designed for New Zealand,” Ginny Andersen said.

“Parents want confidence that their child will leave school able to read, write, communicate, think critically and succeed in modern New Zealand. That requires a coherent curriculum, high expectations and stable settings that schools have the time and support to deliver well.

“Teachers also need the certainty to focus on teaching, rather than constantly scrambling to implement rushed or politically driven changes.

“Whether governments are left or right, curriculum and assessment decisions should be guided by evidence, educational expertise and what will improve learning.

“Governments will continue to set the broad goals and expectations for our education system. That democratic accountability will remain. But detailed curriculum and assessment design should be led by expert educators and assessment specialists, not rewritten according to the preferences of individual Ministers.”

Under Labour:

- The ICCA will be established in legislation to oversee New Zealand’s curriculum and assessment system.
- An interim expert group will be established within Labour’s first three months to provide immediate advice on curriculum and assessment.
- The rollout of curriculum changes that have not yet been implemented will be paused for one year, giving schools breathing room and experts time to assess what should proceed.
- Maths and English work already underway will continue, with appropriate support for schools.
- The current NCEA system will remain in place unchanged until 2029, allowing the Council’s advice to be considered and any future changes to be properly planned and phased in.
- Existing baseline education funding will be reprioritised to establish and operate the Council itself, at an expected cost of $500,000 a year.

“This is not about creating another layer of bureaucracy or going back to square one. It is about building a coherent curriculum, avoiding rushed changes and improving educational outcomes for students,” Ginny Andersen said.

“We will keep what is working, carefully assess changes that are underway and make future decisions based on evidence and expert advice.

“Good curriculum reform takes time. It requires professional expertise, proper implementation and the confidence of the parents, teachers and schools who rely on it.

“Labour will provide the stability and trust our schools and families need. We are inviting National to join us in a bipartisan commitment to protect curriculum and assessment from constant political upheaval.

“Our children deserve an education system that puts their learning first, gives every learner the opportunity to succeed and reflects who we are as New Zealanders.

“Let teachers teach. Let experts do their jobs. And give parents confidence in what their children are learning,” Ginny Andersen said.

documents/release-labour-to-make-it-safe.title: Release: Labour to make it safer for Kiwis online
documents/release-labour-to-make-it-safe.text:
##### Release: Labour to make it safer for Kiwis online

Labour will ensure Kiwis have more control over online content, while strengthening protections for our kids.

“Social media is part of everyday life. It helps us stay connected, share ideas and keep in touch with the people we care about,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“But the big technology companies have too much power over our online experience. At the same time, scams are becoming more sophisticated, fake images and videos are harder to spot, and a lot of parents are worried about what their children are seeing.

“Parents shouldn’t have to take on big tech on their own.

“Labour will put basic rules in place for big technology companies, give people more control over their online experience, and strengthen protections against harmful content,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Ban social media for under-16s. We’ll get current legislation through its first reading and to select committee within our first 100 days, and add strong privacy safeguards on age checks.
- Give you more control of your feed. Everyone will be able to choose between an algorithm-driven feed, or posts only from accounts they follow, and be able to switch back at any time.
- Make platforms responsible for safety. We’ll introduce a new “Digital Duty of Care” law that will require platforms to identify risks and protect Kiwis from harmful content and addictive designs.
- Set up an independent online regulator with the power to fine platforms that break the rules.

“The algorithms deciding what we see are designed to keeping us scrolling, but that’s not always what Kiwis want,” Labour science, technology and innovation spokesperson Reuben Davidson said.

“You might like your recommended feed, and that’s fine, but you should have the choice to switch to seeing only posts from people and accounts you follow.

“Labour will get legislation on the under-16 social media ban moving in our first 100 days, and we’ll make it stronger at select committee with new privacy protections too.

“We’ll join Australia in introducing a new ‘Digital Duty of Care’ law, putting the responsibility of stopping online harm – like bullying, content promoting eating disorders or self-harm, and deepfakes – more on big tech.

“And to enforce these new laws, we will establish an independent online regulator to make sure platforms meet their responsibilities.

“The internet should be a place where people can connect, learn and enjoy themselves.

“New Zealanders have seen the very real harms that occur online, the platforms have had their chance to address it, but they’ve failed to act. It's time for real action to protect young people online.

"Labour is committed to taking that immediate action” Reuben Davidson said.

##### Release: Labour to make power bills more affordable with SolarSaver

Labour will make it easier for more Kiwis to go solar and save on their power bills through SolarSaver, a package that includes:
• Two new Government-backed, long-term, low-interest finance options
• Kickstart subsidies of up to $3,000 for low- and middle-income households
• Easy plug-in options for renters
• A $30 million community battery fund
• Help to find the best option through EECA
• More support for secure, well-paid careers installing solar
"Labour’s SolarSaver will help more Kiwis cut the cost of their household bills by removing the upfront cost that prevents many families from accessing solar," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.
"Renewable energy is the cheapest form of electricity available, but too many households are locked out by the initial cost. SolarSaver creates a simple one-stop shop, provides affordable finance, helps renters access solar for the first time, and offers targeted grants for families who need extra support.
"There's something for everyone. Low- and middle-income households will be eligible for subsidies of up to $3,000. We'll change the rules so renters can use safe plug-in solar panels, saving an estimated $300 to $400 a year. And we'll establish a Community Battery Fund so whole neighbourhoods can share in the benefits of cheaper, cleaner energy," Chris Hipkins said.
"This package is designed to get cheaper electricity into more homes and help New Zealanders save money on their power bills,” Labour Energy and Resources spokesperson Megan Woods said.
"We'll introduce two new low-cost finance options because four out of five households currently cannot access a standard bank green loan.
"Lines companies will be able to offer low-cost loans where solar installations benefit the local network, while a new property-linked finance scheme will allow households to repay costs gradually through their rates bill.
"Renters deserve lower power bills too. We'll modernise the rules for plug-in balcony solar so renters can start saving, and we'll invest in community batteries to help neighbourhoods, marae, and community organisations reduce electricity costs.
"We'll also introduce grants of up to $3,000 for households that need the most help getting started.
"The solar rollout will create local jobs for electricians, installers, and roofers. Alongside our expanded Apprenticeship Boost scheme, Labour will support thousands of young tradies to build careers in a growing industry.
"While National is doubling down on expensive fossil fuels, Labour is focused on helping New Zealanders take control of their power bills through cheaper, cleaner energy," Megan Woods said.

documents/release-labour-will-back-kiwis.text:
##### Release: Labour will back Kiwis and grow the economy

Labour will grow the economy, get the books back into surplus and make sure hard-working New Zealanders can get ahead.

"New Zealand should be a country where hard work gets you somewhere. Where you can get ahead, put down roots and know your kids will have opportunities here," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

"National came in promising to fix the economy. Instead, unemployment is up, businesses are struggling and everything costs more.

"Labour will get the books back into shape but we won’t do it by making life harder for New Zealanders or cutting the services they reply on. You can’t cut your way to growth.

"We’ll invest in the things that make New Zealand stronger – our hospitals and schools, infrastructure, skills and the businesses that create jobs.

"New Zealand has enormous potential. Our job is to back the people and businesses that can realise it, while leaving the country stronger for the next generation," Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Balance the books and return to surplus. Return to original measure of OBEGAL, achieve surplus by 2029/30 and maintain a sustainable fiscal position over the forecast period.

- Bring down debt. We will aim to reduce net debt down to 20% of GDP over time and prioritise investments which support a strong growing economy.

- Keep government spending and revenue sustainable. Core Crown Expenditure and revenue will be maintained at around 33% of GDP when the CGT is fully implemented.

- Strengthen scrutiny of Government spending by establishing an independent Parliamentary Budget Office to analyse Government finances and election commitments.

- Restore the Reserve Bank dual mandate to consider price stability and maximum sustainable employment.

"Labour will be responsible with taxpayers’ money, balancing the books and bringing down debt, while giving New Zealand the capacity to invest in its future," Labour finance and economy spokesperson Barbara Edmonds said.

"Labour will return the books to surplus by 2029/30 and reduce net debt over time but we won't do that by cutting the foundations of our economy.

“Under National unemployment is at an 11-year high, business liquidations are up 71%, homelessness and KiwiSaver hardship withdrawals are at record levels, and public services are under pressure. That isn’t economic success.

"Strong public services are an investment in New Zealand’s future. Labour will make every dollar count, invest where it matters and back the people and businesses that can grow our economy," Barbara Edmonds said.

##### Release: Labour will back Kiwis with a responsible Fiscal Plan

Labour will back New Zealanders to get ahead, grow the economy and make life more affordable, with every promise we have made fully costed and paid for.

“Hard work should get you somewhere. If you work hard and do your bit, you should be able to get ahead and build a good life here in New Zealand,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Too many New Zealanders are falling behind under National. Household budgets are stretched, small businesses are under pressure and the public services people rely on are struggling.

“National promised to grow the economy and get the books in order. It has done neither. 171,000 New Zealanders are unemployed, growth is weaker and debt has continued to rise. They have cut jobs and services, and New Zealanders have been left to pay the price.

“The choice is clear: more cuts and decline under National, or a Labour Government that will balance the books without shrinking the economy, get costs under control and back the people and businesses doing the work.

"Labour will build a country that is better today and better tomorrow,” Chris Hipkins said.

“Every election commitment Labour has made is fully costed and fully funded. The numbers add up and we have left room to confidently respond to whatever comes next,” Labour Finance and Economy spokesperson Barbara Edmonds said.

“We will keep operating allowances at the $2.4 billion set at Budget 2026. Our announced capital commitments fit comfortably within the $12 billion of future capital allowances. We also have almost $10.5 billion of future operating allowances unallocated. We can deliver what we have promised without increasing those allowances.

“We will return the books to surplus in 2028/29 and bring net debt down below 20 percent of GDP over time. We can do that because we have made better choices about where public money goes and will make every dollar work harder.

“New Zealanders deserve a government that looks after their money and backs them to get ahead. Labour has a responsible plan to do both and build a stronger future for New Zealand,” Barbara Edmonds said.

documents/release-labour-will-cut-the-co.title: Release: Labour will cut the cost of getting kids back to school
documents/release-labour-will-cut-the-co.text:
##### Release: Labour will cut the cost of getting kids back to school

Labour will cut back-to-school costs for Kiwi families, starting with cheaper school uniforms and more choice about where parents buy them.

“Getting kids ready for school shouldn’t mean starting the term with another big bill. Families are already stretched, and school costs can push household budgets to the limit,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Parents deserve a fair go. We’ll cut the cost of school uniforms, bring back healthy school lunches and work towards restoring rural school buses, taking pressure off family budgets.

“Cost should never be a barrier to a good education. We’re focused on making life more affordable for families.

“Labour will make school uniforms cheaper by limiting the number of compulsory branded items schools can require and allowing affordable, generic alternatives that meet uniform requirements.

“Families shouldn’t need to turn to hardship support just to get their kids ready for school. We can take practical steps to bring those costs down,” Chris Hipkins said.

Under Labour, schools will be required to:

- Limit the number of compulsory branded uniform items families must buy.
- Allow affordable, non-branded alternatives that meet school uniform requirements.
- Take affordability into account when setting uniform policies.
- Track and publish uniform costs so progress towards making uniforms cheaper can be measured.

“Schools can maintain their identity without forcing parents to pay a premium for a logo. If a plain navy polo does the job, parents shouldn’t have to pay more for the branded version,” Labour education spokesperson Ginny Andersen said.

“I’ve heard from families who get through Christmas only to face another big bill when school starts. Uniforms, lunches, transport - it all adds up.

“Cheaper uniforms are just one part of our plan. Labour will bring back fresh, locally made school lunches from Term 1 2028 and restore the 43 rural school bus routes National cancelled, where possible, working with communities where routes can no longer be reinstated.

“That means lower costs for families, reliable transport for rural kids and healthy lunches that help children learn.

“Getting an education shouldn’t come with a price tag that puts families under pressure. Labour will make school more affordable for parents and better for kids,” Ginny Andersen said.

documents/release-labour-will-get-emerge.text:
##### Release: Labour will get emergency departments moving

Labour will start fixing overcrowded emergency departments, with more nurses, faster access to hospital beds and more people getting care before they need to go to the ED.

“Patients are waiting too long, emergency departments are overcrowded, and nurses and doctors are under enormous pressure. Labour has a plan to fix it,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“National has hired just 54 nurses in two years while hospitals struggle to cope and newly qualified nurses can’t find jobs. That’s not good enough.

“Labour will get more nurses into the health system, make it easier to see a GP, get patients into hospital beds faster and help more people get urgent care close to home,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour’s plan has four priorities:

- moving patients through hospital faster
- getting people the right care in the right place
- keeping people healthy and out of hospital,
- stronger leadership from day one

“Serious delays in ED often happen because there is a lack of beds in hospital wards, creating a backlog in the emergency room,” Labour Health spokesperson Dr Ayesha Verrall said.

“Labour will stop avoidable delays. We’ll tackle staffing and discharge bottlenecks, prepare hospitals for winter before demand surges, and fund teams to help older people recover safely at home.

“We’ll order an immediate report identifying hospital beds that could be opened with the right staffing and make hospitals accountable for getting patients the care they need. The report will also look into deaths and safety linked to long waits.

“Not everyone who needs urgent care needs a hospital. We’ll train more extended-care paramedics to treat people safely at home or in the community, connect frontline health professionals with urgent-care and emergency specialists, and help people access the medicines they need.

“We’ll also tackle the pressure before people reach the emergency department. Three free GP visits a year through our Medicard, free prescriptions, more GP appointments and more local clinics will help people get treatment earlier, before manageable health problems become emergencies.

“We’ll end National’s hiring freeze and guarantee every eligible New Zealand-trained graduate nurse a job in our health system. Around 2,400 graduates a year will be offered work, with roles available from 2027.

“New Zealanders deserve emergency care when they need it, not hours waiting in an overcrowded department. Labour’s plan will help people get care earlier, get treated faster and recover closer to home,” Ayesha Verrall said.

documents/release-labour-will-get-kiwis-.title: Release: Labour will get Kiwis a better deal from banks
documents/release-labour-will-get-kiwis-.text:
##### Release: Labour will get Kiwis a better deal from banks

Labour will open up New Zealand’s banking sector to more competition, giving Kiwis more choice and making the big banks work harder for their business.

“This election is about the cost of living. Almost every Kiwi relies on a bank to get paid, pay the bills, buy a home or grow a business,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Four big banks dominate our banking sector. When there isn’t enough competition, customers have less choice and banks have less reason to offer them a better deal.

“Labour will break down the barriers that stop new competitors taking on the big banks.

“When banks compete harder, Kiwis get more choice and more power to shop around for a better deal,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Give Kiwis more choice: Introduce a new e-money licence for businesses offering services like digital wallets and payments, with rules that reflect what they do and the risks involved.
- Open up the banking system: Make sure smaller providers can access essential banking and payments infrastructure on fair terms.
- Give Kiwis 24/7 access to their money: Require a secure, 24-hour, seven-day-a-week real-time payments system by 2030.
- Back new competitors: Create a clearer pathway for innovative financial providers to grow into genuine banking competitors.
- Make it easier to switch: Make government-verified identity easier to use across banks and fintechs, reducing the hassle of signing up or switching.

“The big four banks hold around 85 to 90 percent of registered bank assets. For most Kiwis, that means too few real choices about who they bank with and what services they use,” Labour Commerce spokesperson Arena Williams said.

“Technology has changed what’s possible. You shouldn’t have to rely on one of the big banks for every financial service you use, and new providers with a better offer should have a fair chance to win your business.

“Labour will make it easier for new providers to get started, grow and access the systems they need to compete. If the big banks won’t provide fair access, we’ll step in.

“We’ll modernise our payments system too. Kiwis should be able to move their own money when they need to, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and if you find a better deal switching providers shouldn’t be a hassle.

“Kiwibank has an important role too. Labour created it and we’ll keep it 100 percent New Zealand-owned. But one challenger isn’t enough – Kiwis deserve more competition and more choice across banking.

“National promised to shake up banking but three years later, the big four are still calling the shots.

“Labour will open up the system, bring in new competition and give Kiwis more power to choose,” Arena Williams said.

documents/release-labour-will-make-ai-wo.title: Release: Labour will make AI work for New Zealanders
documents/release-labour-will-make-ai-wo.text:
##### Release: Labour will make AI work for New Zealanders

Labour will make sure New Zealand is ready to seize the opportunities AI presents, manage the risks and ensure people benefit from the technology.

“AI is changing how we work, access services and make decisions, Labour will make sure it works for Kiwis," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

"Used well, AI has huge benefits. It can cut hospital paperwork so doctors and nurses have more time with patients. Workers and small businesses can be more productive. Certain services can be delivered more efficiently.

“But we cannot leave it to big international tech companies to decide how it shapes our future. Labour has a plan to make AI work for New Zealanders, not just the companies that build and own it,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour's AI Action Plan will:

- Establish an Office of AI to coordinate AI policy across government.
- Establish an online safety regulator within the Department for Internal Affairs.
- Develop a copyright framework so creators control and are paid for their work.
- Set clear rules for data centres so households aren't left carrying the cost.
- Support small businesses and community organisations to adopt AI safely.
- Establish an AI in Education team to support schools, teachers and students.
- Work with businesses and unions to make sure productivity gains show up in wages and conditions.

“New Zealanders can see the opportunities of AI, but they also see the risks, whether that's job losses, harmful content, data centres driving up energy costs, or a lack of accountability for important decisions that affect people's lives,” Labour science, technology and innovation spokesperson Reuben Davidson said.

"Labour will protect what matters, unlock the benefits, and make sure New Zealand sets the rules on its own terms. That means protecting peoples’ rights, safety and privacy, creative work, and ensuring that there is always human accountability.

“We'll also make big data centres pay their own way, securing their own renewable energy and covering their own connection costs. New Zealand households shouldn't be subsidising the power bills of overseas tech companies.

"We can't afford three more years of National letting big tech call all the shots. It's time New Zealand set its own rules, so that all New Zealanders benefit," Reuben Davidson said.

documents/release-labour-will-make-price.title: Release: Labour will make price gouging illegal
documents/release-labour-will-make-price.text:
##### Release: Labour will make price gouging illegal

Labour will crack down on companies who charge New Zealanders excessive prices for essential goods and services.

"New Zealanders are working hard, but they’re still going backwards. Christopher Luxon promised he’d fix the cost of living, but he’s just made it worse, all while a handful of big companies price gouge households - charging whatever they like for the things families can't do without," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

"Right now, a company big enough to dodge competition can charge excessive prices for the basics, like food and fuel, and there's no law against it. Labour will change that, by making it illegal for big powerful companies to rip off New Zealanders on the essentials," Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Make it illegal for big companies with substantial market power to charge excessive prices for essential goods and services, or to pay unfairly low prices to suppliers.
- Set a clear legal test for the first time: prices well above what they would otherwise be in a competitive market, sustained over time.
- Give the Commerce Commission the power to investigate price gouging and back groups representing consumers and suppliers to do the same
- Require companies that gouge to pay penalties and hand back every dollar of excess profit.

“Nearly one in three New Zealand households couldn't afford enough food last year. Since National took office, the price of butter has gone up 58 percent, bread is up 45 percent, and mince is up 30 percent,” Labour Commerce and Consumer Affairs spokesperson Arena Williams said.

“Meanwhile, the growers who put food on our shelves get squeezed by the big players just as hard as the families buying it.

"Labour’s policy will ensure that companies with significant market power are charging a fair price for the things that your family can't do without.

“This is aimed at a small number of very large companies, it won't touch the 97 percent of New Zealand businesses that are small, like your local dairy or cafe.

“It also only applies in markets for essentials, like food, power, fuel, transport, telecommunications banking, and insurance.

"Rules like these already operate in the United Kingdom, Europe, Canada, and Australia. It's time New Zealanders had the same protection.

“Christopher Luxon is too out of touch to realise that families can’t even afford the basics under his policies. Households are working harder just to keep up, while the biggest companies post record profits off excessive prices.

“A Labour Government will work to make your life easier and more affordable. This election is about the cost of living and New Zealanders can't afford another three years of National," Arena Williams said.

##### Release: Labour will restore Te Tiriti commitment in schools

A future Labour Government will restore the commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi in Aotearoa New Zealand’s schooling system.

“Today, I have submitted my members bill, the Education and Training (Upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi) Amendment Bill, to reinstate the obligation for school boards to give effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi,” Labour spokesperson for Māori education Willow Jean Prime said.

“Schools have been clear: honouring Te Tiriti in education matters. It helps create inclusive schools where every child feels valued, respected, and reflected in the classroom.

“Labour will reverse the damage this Government has done to Māori education. We will restore a clear legal commitment to Te Tiriti in our schools, and this bill is the first step.

“Schools are tired of the Government’s attacks on Māori education – from cutting support for teachers learning te reo Māori, then it was removing books with Te Reo words, and eventually they came for Te Tiriti.

“Māori have fought hard for equity, and we cannot afford to go backwards.

“We'll work in partnership with schools, kura and communities so that commitments to Te Tiriti in law translate into real change in classrooms, which mean better resources, stronger local partnerships, and more confidence for teachers.

“Labour is clear: Te Tiriti o Waitangi belongs in our schools. A future Labour Government will restore that commitment back where it belongs,” Willow-Jean Prime said.

documents/release-labour-will-strengthen.text:
##### Release: Labour will strengthen KiwiSaver for future generations

Labour will make KiwiSaver work harder for more New Zealanders, helping Kiwis save, build wealth and retire with security.

"Labour is the party of KiwiSaver. We believe every New Zealander should have the opportunity to build a secure future," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

"Sir Michael Cullen turned that belief into KiwiSaver, while National voted against it. Today KiwiSaver funds exceed $138 billion and are an important source of investment in our economy.

"Under National too many New Zealanders are struggling to pay the bills, let alone save for tomorrow. More than a million working-age KiwiSaver members aren’t contributing at all, while 83,400 are on a savings suspension.

“New Zealanders cannot afford another three years of going backwards. Labour will get our economy growing again so working people can build something for their future.

"KiwiSaver is one of Labour’s proudest legacies. We created it, and now we’re going to make it work better for people," Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Make employer contributions compulsory, and lift to 6 percent by 2032, including when employees reduce or pause their own contributions.
- Set the employee default at 4 percent, remove the minimum contribution rate, and give employees more flexibility to choose their rate as circumstances change.
- Ban new total remuneration contracts that absorb employer KiwiSaver contributions into salaries.
- Extend employer contributions to workers over 65.
- Keep KiwiSaver growing for parents while they’re on paid parental leave.
- Explore more flexible KiwiSaver options for self-employed New Zealanders.

"Labour built KiwiSaver and changed the way New Zealanders save. Now we want it to work harder for more people," Labour finance and economy spokesperson Barbara Edmonds said.

"National has made it harder for Kiwis to save and now wants to force workers to put more in. Labour will require employers to contribute at the same amount as National is proposing but give workers more flexibility when money is tight.

“We’ll also make KiwiSaver fairer for parents, older Kiwis and broaden who benefits – working with self-employed New Zealanders on more flexible ways to build their savings in the scheme.

“From 1 July 2028, employer contributions will become compulsory and will extend to paid parental leave and workers over 65. We’ll phase changes across our KiwiSaver policy carefully, giving workers and businesses certainty.

"Stronger KiwiSaver means more wealth in Kiwi hands and more investment here at home. Labour will back Kiwis to save and back the businesses that will grow our economy," Barbara Edmonds said.

documents/release-labours-plan-for-faire.text:
##### Release: Labour's plan for fairer grocery prices

Labour will take immediate action to increase competition in the grocery sector, giving New Zealanders more choice and fairer prices at the checkout.

"This election is about the cost of living and who will take real action to get it under control. Families are paying too much for groceries, and Labour has a plan to bring prices down," Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“A Labour Government will crack down on big companies ripping you off, and we’ll take immediate action on grocery prices.

“The time for reviews is over. Only Labour will make grocery prices fairer and lower your weekly grocery bills,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Open up the market by requiring Woolworths and Foodstuffs to run their­­ wholesale supply businesses independently from their retail stores.
- Guarantee Kiwi grocers the right to buy their stock from any wholesaler they choose, on fair terms.
- Free small grocers like Four Square operators from their restraints of trade, by voiding anti-competitive arrangements that keep their prices high.
- Ban junk fees charged to suppliers
- Make rebate and data deals more transparent

"New Zealand has lots of supermarket brands, but most are owned by just two groups: Woolworths and Foodstuffs. Together, they control more than 80 percent of the grocery market,” Labour Commerce and Consumer Affairs spokesperson Arena Williams said.

“The big supermarkets can favour their own retail stores, meaning smaller shops and independent supermarkets end up paying more. That makes it harder for them to compete and offer you a better deal.

“National promised to fix the cost of living and bring grocery prices down. Instead, mince is up 36 percent since they took office. Bread has jumped 66 percent, butter is up 72 percent, beef mince 36 percent, cheese 31 percent, and milk 33 percent.

“Despite talking big, National has had three years and done nothing. Now, with the election only weeks away, they say what we need is another review. New Zealanders can't eat a review. It's time for real action.

“Only Labour will act decisively. We will open the market so more supermarkets can offer lower prices, giving shoppers more choice and a better deal at the checkout.

“These changes will put money back in people’s pockets. Our grocery plan will deliver lasting change by giving shoppers more choice and ensure fairer prices that last.

“Better now. Fairer grocery prices for the future. Better starts now,” Arena Williams said.

documents/release-labours-plan-to-bring-.title: Release: Labour's plan to bring down costs for Kiwis
documents/release-labours-plan-to-bring-.text:
##### Release: Labour's plan to bring down costs for Kiwis

Labour has released its Cost of Living Action Plan, with help for families on food bills, healthcare costs, petrol, transport, and the cost of getting kids to school.

“Everywhere I go I hear the same thing: people are working hard, but they’re still finding less left at the end of each week. That's why getting the cost of living under control is Labour’s number one priority,” Labour Leader Chris Hipkins said.

“The weekly groceries. Seeing a doctor. Power bills. Petrol. It all adds up. Christopher Luxon promised to fix the cost of living, but under National things have gotten worse. New Zealand can’t afford another three years of National making life harder and more expensive.

“Labour has a plan. We’ll help with the bills you face every week, and we’ll crack down on big companies ripping you off, so you get a fairer deal.

“Getting costs under control is also about making sure people have enough money coming in, which is why our plan is about good jobs too. We’ll back apprentices and tradies, and get work started fixing our schools and hospitals,” Chris Hipkins said.

Labour will:

- Give every New Zealander three free GP visits a year with a new Medicard
- Cap public transport fares at $20 a week in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, and $10 everywhere else
- Freeze the fuel tax for three years
- Help households install solar, with low-interest SolarSaver loans
- Make price gouging on essentials illegal, and make companies pay back what they’ve overcharged
- Scrap the $5 prescription charge
- Crack down on hidden fees, subscription traps and junk insurance
- Give smaller Kiwi businesses, from independent mechanics to local grocers, a fair shot against the big players
- Cut student debt by 10%, and back 30,000 apprentices into work
- Bring back fresh, locally made school lunches, and work to restore rural school buses

“Three free doctors visits could save a couple up to $500 a year. A daily bus commuter could save around $25 a week. And a family with solar could cut around $1,000 a year off their power bill,” Chris Hipkins said.

“These are real savings for real people. And every promise we’ve made is fully costed and paid for in our fiscal plan.

“Today, I am also announcing two new commitments to help parents with household costs. Labour will bring back fresh, locally-made school lunches, and we will work to restore the rural school bus routes that National cut.

“As a parent myself, I know how school costs add up. Labour’s school lunches will mean one less meal to find money for and a healthy lunch for your children. It also means more jobs in your local community.

“And bringing back rural school buses that National cancelled will save parents on petrol costs, not to mention time and stress.

“Kiwis should be able to put food on the table, see a doctor and get where they need to go, with something left over at the end of the week. Your hard work should get you somewhere.

“Lower bills. Good jobs. A fairer deal. That’s Labour’s plan,” Chris Hipkins said.

### Release: Labour's plan to bring down costs for Kiwis

##### Release: Move on Bill still punishes the homeless

The select committee's changes to National’s move on orders Bill are a significant win for New Zealanders, but the Bill still continues to criminalise people for being homeless.

"National’s Bill was cruel and unworkable as introduced. It wanted Police to respond to a 14-year-old living alone on the street with a move on order, a fine, and the threat of imprisonment. How can that be our response to a seeing a child live on the street?” Labour justice spokesperson Camilla Belich said.

"More than 7000 New Zealanders made submissions, with more than 98 percent opposing the Bill. That included the Police Association, Retail NZ, City Missions, faith groups, and everyday New Zealanders. They should take enormous credit for the changes that have been made.

“But the fundamental problem remains. Criminalising people for sleeping rough when they have no other option is wrong, and it shows just how out of touch Christopher Luxon is.

“The Bill does nothing to address the underlying problem of homelessness. National stopped Kāinga Ora from making more homes available, stopped people in need from accessing emergency housing, and made the cost of living worse.

"You don't fix homelessness by telling people to move on, you fix it by ensuring people have access to stable housing.

"Labour will advance amendments at committee stage to remove rough sleeping and begging from this Bill entirely, and we hope parties across the House will support them.

"New Zealanders have made it very clear this Bill is not the solution to our housing crisis that National made worse. We simply can't afford three more years of National treating people as problems to be swept under the rug," Camilla Belich said.

##### Release: Targeted tax to grow the economy and fund free doctor’s visits

- A targeted capital gains tax on the profit made after 1 July 2027 when a commercial property or residential property (excluding the family home) is sold.
- The family home, farms, KiwiSaver, shares, business assets, inheritances, and personal items will be exempt.
- Nine out of 10 New Zealanders won’t pay tax on the property they own, and everyone will get three free visits a year to the doctor.

Labour will grow the economy for everyone, back Kiwi businesses, and fund three free doctor’s visits a year for every New Zealander.

“Right now, our tax system rewards property speculation instead of the people creating jobs and growing the economy. We will change that,” Labour leader Chris Hipkins said.

“Our simple, targeted tax changes will make sure those profiting from property pay their fair share, leveling the playing field for Kiwi businesses and innovation.

“Every dollar raised will go straight into the health system, including funding three free doctor’s visits a year for everyone with a new Medicard. This will save New Zealanders money every year.

“Because it’s part of our plan to deliver a better economy for Kiwi families, our targeted capital gains tax completely exempts the family home, farms, KiwiSaver, shares, business assets, inheritances, and any other personal items.

“Christopher Luxon promised to fix the economy and protect public services, but he is making it worse. Only Labour will grow the economy, support Kiwi businesses, and rebuild the health system,” Chris Hipkins said.

“No one should have to choose between seeing a doctor and putting food on the table, but that’s the reality for far too many New Zealanders,” Labour health spokesperson Ayesha Verrall said.

“One in six New Zealanders cannot afford to visit their doctor when they are sick. Some doctors' fees are heading towards $100 a visit. That hasn’t happened by accident. It is a direct result of Christopher Luxon’s cuts to healthcare and tax breaks for tobacco companies and property speculators.

“Our plan means that every New Zealander will get a new Medicard that they can use to access three free doctor’s visits each year at their enrolled practice.

“This election is make-or-break for our health system. Under a Labour Government, all someone will need to see their doctor is a Medicard, not their credit card,” Ayesha Verrall said.

By LabourVoices

## Chris Hipkins promises to reverse pay equity changes in first 100 days if elected

Anna Sargent

Caption:Chris Hipkins meets a member of the public at a community meeting in Spreydon.Photo credit:RNZ / Anna Sargent

Chris Hipkins has made a campaign commitment to reverse pay equity changes in the first 100 days of a Labour government, during a packed public meeting in Christchurch.

The Labour leader received a standing ovation walking into a community hall in Spreydon on Monday night where close to 200 people filled the room, with some spilling out the doors.

The meeting was held a day after Labour launched its campaign, promising "plenty more fire" this election.

Hipkins received a warm reception, and many of his answers were met with applause.

"It's great to see the energy that is going to propel our campaign to victory," he told the room.

Labour leader Chris Hipkins spoke to a packed public meeting in Spreydon on Monday 28 September, 2026.

RNZ / Anna Sargent

One of the biggest cheers of the night came after a question by a support worker on Labour's stance on restoring pay equity.

Hipkins said Labour would quickly reverse pay equity law changes if elected.

"I think probably the most reprehensible thing I have seen in my time as a member of Parliament was the government's decision last year with no notice, with no warning, with no consultation, to pass under urgency a law that cancelled pay equity for tens of thousands of women," Hipkins said.

"I want to give you a reassurance that within the first 100 days we are back in government we will reverse that change.

"When we have reversed that change, care and support workers will be the first in the queue to sit down with to get a settlement because you've waited long enough."

Hipkins was asked by a 13-year-old girl what was the most important thing his government would do to support women and girls in New Zealand, to which he said "restoring pay equity".

Hipkins received a warm reception, and many of his answers were met with applause.

RNZ / Anna Sargent

Hipkins said this election was a cost-of-living election and repeated the line to the crowd that the country "cannot afford three more years of this government".

He promoted Labour's policies including the SolarSaver programme, the apprenticeship boost and cutting student loan debt.

For about an hour the crowd asked a gamut of questions, touching on healthcare, housing, pay equity, AI and local government.

Attendees RNZ spoke to after the meeting were impressed by Hipkins.

A nurse at Christchurch Hospital, who did not wish to be named, said Hipkins had given him hope.

"It's nice to have a future prime minister who is human. We've got a prime minister at the moment where the two tails are wagging the dog. We've got a leader here," he said.

One woman said there was not a single thing said she disagreed with.

"This is the first time I've felt hope for a long time. I think his integrity and what the Labour Party is trying to do for every Kiwi came through," she said.

Hipkins has promised to explain how Labour's promises will be paid for after the government opens its books on Tuesday, after which the party will need to crunch the numbers.
